title: Agent evaluation
sections:
Agent evaluation
An agent's score depends on the system, the tasks and the protocol together. A task is one problem; a trial is one attempt at it; the trajectory is everything the agent did along the way.

Reliability
If one attempt succeeds with probability $p$, the chance that at least one of $k$ attempts succeeds is $\mathrm{pass@}k = 1 - (1-p)^k$, while the chance that all $k$ succeed is $\mathrm{pass}^k = p^k$. With $p = 0.8$ and $k = 3$ these are $99.2\%$ and $51.2\%$.

Estimating from trials
With $n$ trials and $c$ successes, an unbiased estimate is $$\widehat{\mathrm{pass}^k} = \frac{\binom{c}{k}}{\binom{n}{k}}$$ Proof sketch: pick $k$ of the $n$ trials uniformly at random. The chance that every picked trial succeeded is the number of all-success subsets, $\binom{c}{k}$, over the number of subsets, $\binom{n}{k}$; averaging over the picks gives exactly $p^k$ in expectation.
